description: Crunchy - All-in-one clean living app for Gen Z women. React Native (Expo) + Supabase + TypeScript + NativeWind.

userStories.title: Project setup with Expo, TypeScript, NativeWind, and Expo Router
userStories.description: As a developer, I need the base project scaffolded so all future stories have a foundation to build on.
acceptanceCriteria: Create Expo project with TypeScript template using create-expo-app
Install and configure expo-router for file-based navigation
Install and configure NativeWind (Tailwind CSS for React Native)
Set up bottom tab navigation with 5 tabs: Home, Scan, Explore, Community, Profile
Each tab shows a placeholder screen with the tab name
App compiles and runs without errors (npx expo start works)
Tailwind classes render correctly on at least one screen
userStories.notes: Use Expo SDK 52+. Use expo-router v4. Design system colors: sage green #8B9E7C, peach #F4A574, off-white #FAF8F5, dark text #2D2D2D. Rounded-2xl cards, soft shadows.

userStories.title: Design system and shared components
userStories.description: As a developer, I need reusable UI components so all screens look consistent and beautiful.
acceptanceCriteria: Create tailwind.config.js with custom colors (sage, peach, cream, dark), border radius, shadows
Create shared Button component (primary, secondary, outline variants)
Create shared Card component with rounded-2xl, shadow, padding
Create shared Header component
Create shared SafeAreaWrapper component
Create shared Badge component (green/yellow/red for Clean/Caution/Avoid ratings)
All components use NativeWind classes
App compiles without errors
userStories.notes: Think modern, clean, Gen Z aesthetic. Soft greens and warm neutrals. No harsh colors. The app should feel like a breath of fresh air.

userStories.title: Welcome and onboarding screens
userStories.description: As a new user, I want a beautiful welcome experience so I understand what the app does and feel excited to use it.
acceptanceCriteria: Welcome screen with app logo/name, tagline 'The operating system for conscious living', and CTA button
3-screen onboarding carousel showing key features (Scan, Discover, Connect)
Each carousel screen has illustration placeholder, title, and subtitle
Skip button and dot indicators on carousel
Final screen leads to quiz or sign up
Smooth swipe animations between screens
App compiles without errors
userStories.notes: Use react-native-reanimated for smooth carousel animations. Keep copy short and punchy. No em-dashes.

userStories.title: Crunchy Score Quiz
userStories.description: As a new user, I want to take a fun quiz to find out how 'crunchy' I am so I get personalized recommendations and a shareable result.
acceptanceCriteria: 10 multiple-choice questions about lifestyle habits (food, skincare, cleaning, clothing, mindset)
Swipeable question cards with progress bar at top
Each question has 3-4 answer options with icons/emojis
Animated score calculation on completion
Result screen showing score 1-100 with label (Seedling/Sprout/Blooming/Thriving/Fully Rooted)
Beautiful shareable result card designed for social media stories
Share button that opens native share sheet
CTA to create account after results
Quiz can be taken without an account
App compiles without errors
userStories.notes: This is the viral loop. The result card MUST look stunning when shared. Use react-native-view-shot to capture the result card as an image. Questions should be fun and relatable, not clinical.

userStories.title: Authentication screens
userStories.description: As a user, I want to sign up and log in so my data persists across sessions.
acceptanceCriteria: Sign up screen with email/password fields
Login screen with email/password fields
Google OAuth button (UI ready, can be mocked)
Apple Sign-In button (UI ready, can be mocked)
Form validation with clear error messages
Loading states on buttons
Link between sign up and login screens
Auth state management (context or zustand)
Protected routes: redirect to auth if not logged in
For now, use mock auth (store in AsyncStorage) since Supabase isn't connected yet
App compiles without errors
userStories.notes: Keep the auth screens on-brand (sage green, warm). No generic-looking auth forms.

userStories.title: Home screen
userStories.description: As a logged-in user, I want a home screen that gives me quick access to scanning and shows personalized content.
acceptanceCriteria: Greeting with user's name and crunchy score badge
Large prominent Scan button (center of attention)
Clean Swap of the Day card with product image, name, why to swap, and alternative
Quick stats row: total scans, crunchy score, saved items count
Trending in Community section showing 2-3 preview cards
Pull-to-refresh functionality
All data can be mock/seed data for now
App compiles without errors
userStories.notes: The scan button should be unmissable. Think of it as the primary CTA of the entire app. Use haptic feedback on tap.

userStories.title: Product scanner with barcode scanning
userStories.description: As a user, I want to scan a product barcode so I can instantly see if it contains harmful ingredients.
acceptanceCriteria: Camera viewfinder screen using expo-camera
Request camera permissions with friendly explanation
Barcode detection using expo-camera barcode scanner
Scan mode toggle UI (Barcode / Label / Product) even if only barcode works initially
On barcode detection: vibrate/haptic + navigate to result screen
Recent scans list below camera when not actively scanning
Flashlight toggle button
App compiles without errors
userStories.notes: Use expo-camera and expo-barcode-scanner. Add expo-haptics for feedback on scan.

userStories.title: Scan result screen
userStories.description: As a user, after scanning a product I want to see a clear toxin rating with ingredient breakdown and alternatives.
acceptanceCriteria: Product header: name, brand, image, category
Overall rating badge: Clean (green), Caution (yellow), Avoid (red) with large icon
Ingredient list with each ingredient color-coded (safe=green, concern=yellow, toxic=red)
Tappable ingredients that expand to show plain-English explanation of why it's flagged
Alternatives section: horizontal scrollable cards showing clean alternative products
Each alternative card: product image, name, price, rating, buy button
DIY Instead button (links to recipe if available)
Share button that generates a shareable result card image
Save to favorites button
Uses mock data for now (create realistic seed data for 20+ products)
App compiles without errors
userStories.notes: This screen needs to be information-dense but not overwhelming. Progressive disclosure: show rating first, details on tap. The alternatives carousel should feel like shopping.

userStories.title: Explore and alternatives browse screen
userStories.description: As a user, I want to browse clean product alternatives by category so I can discover new products.
acceptanceCriteria: Search bar at top of screen
Category grid: Food, Skincare, Cleaning, Personal Care, Clothing, Home (with icons)
Tapping a category shows filtered product list
Product cards with: image, name, brand, rating badge, price
Filter bar: price range, certifications, rating
Tapping a product opens its detail/scan result screen
Save/favorite button on each card
Seed data: at least 30 products across categories
App compiles without errors
userStories.notes: Make the category icons fun and on-brand. Think emoji-style or minimal illustrations.

userStories.title: DIY recipe library
userStories.description: As a user, I want to browse DIY recipes for clean alternatives so I can make my own products.
acceptanceCriteria: Recipe list screen with cards: photo, title, difficulty stars, time, cost estimate
Category tabs: Cleaning, Skincare, Haircare, Home, Personal Care
Filter by: difficulty (Easy/Medium/Hard), time, category
Full recipe detail screen: hero image, ingredients list with quantities, numbered steps, tips section, cost vs store-bought comparison
Save recipe to favorites
Mark as 'Made It' button with counter showing how many users made it
Seed data: at least 30 recipes across categories with realistic content
App compiles without errors
userStories.notes: Recipes should feel like a clean, modern recipe blog. Big hero images, clear steps. Include real-sounding recipe content (e.g., 'All-Purpose Citrus Cleaner', 'Honey Oat Face Mask').

userStories.title: Community feed
userStories.description: As a user, I want a social feed where I can see what other crunchy girls are sharing and post my own content.
acceptanceCriteria: Feed screen showing posts in chronological order
Post card: avatar, username, timestamp, text content, optional image, like count, comment count
Like button with animation
Comment button opens comment sheet
Hashtag rendering (tappable, colored)
Trending hashtags bar at top
Create post FAB (floating action button)
Create post screen: text input, image picker, hashtag suggestions
Seed data: at least 15 realistic community posts
App compiles without errors
userStories.notes: Keep it Reddit-lite meets Instagram. Clean cards, not cluttered. The community should feel warm and supportive.

userStories.title: Profile screen
userStories.description: As a user, I want to see my profile with my crunchy score, scan history, and saved items.
acceptanceCriteria: Profile header: avatar, username, crunchy score badge with label
Stats row: total scans, recipes made, days active
Tab sections: Scan History, Saved Items, My Posts
Scan History: list of past scans with product name, date, rating
Saved Items: grid of saved products and recipes
My Posts: list of community posts by this user
Settings gear icon in header
Settings screen: account info, notification toggles, subscription status, about, logout
App compiles without errors
userStories.notes: The crunchy score badge should be prominent and feel like an achievement. Think gamification.

userStories.title: Subscription paywall screen
userStories.description: As a user, I want to see subscription options so I can upgrade for premium features.
acceptanceCriteria: Paywall screen showing 3 tiers: Free, Starter ($9.99/mo), Premium ($19.99/mo)
Feature comparison list for each tier
Highlight recommended tier (Starter)
Subscribe buttons (mocked for now, no real payment)
Paywall triggered when free user hits scan limit (5/day) or tries premium feature
Close/dismiss button
Restore purchases link
Beautiful design that sells the value, not just lists features
App compiles without errors
userStories.notes: Make this screen convert. Show the value, not just the price. Use social proof ('Join 10,000+ crunchy girls'). No pressure, but make premium feel worth it.

userStories.title: Supabase database schema and migrations
userStories.description: As a developer, I need the complete database schema ready so we can connect the app to a real backend.
acceptanceCriteria: Create supabase/migrations/ directory with SQL migration files
Tables: users (extends auth.users), products, alternatives, scans, recipes, recipe_ingredients, recipe_steps, posts, comments, follows, saved_items, quiz_results
Row Level Security policies on all tables
Proper indexes on frequently queried columns
Foreign key relationships correctly defined
Seed data SQL file with realistic products, recipes, and sample posts
Schema matches all the data models used in the app
Migration files are numbered and ordered correctly
userStories.notes: Use UUIDs for all primary keys. Include created_at and updated_at on all tables. Products table should support all categories: food, skincare, cleaning, personal care, clothing, home.

userStories.title: Label OCR scanning mode
userStories.description: As a user, I want to photograph a product's ingredient label so the app can read and analyze the ingredients even without a barcode.
acceptanceCriteria: Label scan mode in scanner: user takes a photo of ingredient list
Photo capture UI with frame guide overlay showing where to position the label
Loading state while processing ('Reading ingredients...')
OCR result screen showing detected ingredients with toxin analysis
If OCR fails or is unclear, show friendly error with retry option
For MVP: mock the OCR processing but build the full UI flow
Result feeds into the same scan result screen as barcode scanning
App compiles without errors
userStories.notes: The frame guide should help users position the label correctly. Think of how document scanners work. Include a 'tips for best results' helper.

userStories.title: AI product recognition scanning mode
userStories.description: As a user, I want to point my camera at any product (no barcode or label needed) and have the app identify it and find its ingredients.
acceptanceCriteria: Product scan mode in scanner: user takes a photo of the product itself
Photo capture with 'Point at the product' overlay text
Loading state while AI processes ('Identifying product...')
Confirmation screen: 'Is this [Product Name]?' with Yes/No
If confirmed, show full scan result with ingredients and rating
If wrong, option to search manually
For MVP: mock the AI recognition but build the complete UI flow
Works for clothing (shows fabric tag analysis), bottles (shows material analysis), any product
App compiles without errors
userStories.notes: This is the premium-tier feature. Show a subtle 'Premium' badge on this scan mode. The confirmation step is critical to avoid wrong product matches.

userStories.title: Polish, animations, and empty states
userStories.description: As a user, I want the app to feel polished and delightful with smooth animations, proper loading states, and helpful empty states.
acceptanceCriteria: Screen transition animations (smooth slide/fade)
Button press animations (scale down slightly)
Like button heart animation
Scan success animation (checkmark burst)
Loading skeletons on all list screens
Empty states for: no scans yet, no saved items, no posts, no search results
Each empty state has an illustration/icon, message, and CTA
Pull-to-refresh on all scrollable screens
Haptic feedback on key actions (scan, like, save)
App compiles without errors
userStories.notes: Use react-native-reanimated for animations. Use expo-haptics for haptic feedback. Empty states should be encouraging, not depressing ('Start your clean living journey by scanning your first product!').

userStories.title: Interest selection and personalization
userStories.description: As a new user after taking the quiz, I want to select my interests so the app can personalize my experience.
acceptanceCriteria: Interest selection screen shown after quiz/signup
Categories with toggle chips: Food & Beverages, Skincare & Beauty, Cleaning Products, Personal Care, Clothing & Textiles, Home & Living, Baby Products
Minimum 2 selections required
Selected interests influence home screen content (swap of the day category, trending posts)
Interests saved to user profile
Can be edited later from profile settings
App compiles without errors
userStories.notes: Make the chips visually appealing with icons. This data is valuable for personalization and will drive engagement.
